scenes.narration: Did 3.0% of all US workers really quit their jobs in one month?
In November 2021, the monthly quit rate spiked to 3.0%, the highest level ever recorded.
Just eighteen months before that, lockdowns froze the market, plunging the quit rate to 1.5% in April 2020.
By September 2026, the quit rate cooled by -30% from that historic high, settling back at 2.1%.
Workers traded uncertainty for massive career leverage. The full story is on the channel.
Did workers actually win the wage war over the last decade?
Between January 2015 and October 2026, average hourly pay surged by +57% for non-managers.
Hourly wages climbed from $20.80 in January 2015 all the way to an all-time high of $32.75 in October 2026.
Even since January 2020, pay jumped +37%, fueled by intense competition for staff.
Quitting handed employees permanent bargaining power. The full story is on the channel.
How did US unemployment drop by -72% so quickly?
In April 2020, US unemployment hit a terrifying peak of 14.8% as lockdowns shut down the economy.
Yet hiring rebounded so fast that joblessness plummeted to a record low of 3.4% by April 2023.
By October 2026, the rate stood at 4.1%, a -72% collapse from that pandemic peak.
Extreme labor shortages completely flipped the balance of power. The full story is on the channel.
